specification.userPrompt: Create a new project for this work (e.g. `Tank Combat Arcade`) and build a top-down tank combat arcade game there. Write the entire game as a single self-contained file at `workspace/index.html` IN THAT NEW PROJECT (HTML + inline `<style>` + inline `<script>`, no external assets, no build step). The player controls a tank with arrow keys (or WASD), fires projectiles with space, and fights at least one enemy tank. Track a score on screen. Make keyboard input observable in the browser: expose `window.gameState = gameState` or update a `document.body.dataset.inputTick` value inside key handlers so automated runtime checks can see input activity. The first concrete deliverable is the index.html file inside the new project — write it now. TANK_COMBAT_HTML_SHAPE: write one complete `index.html` document in a single workspace `write_file` call. Use exactly this source shape: `<!doctype html><html><head><style>...</style></head><body>...<canvas id="game"></canvas>...<script>/* all game JavaScript here */</script></body></html>`. All JavaScript must be inside that one inline `<script>` block before `</body>`: declarations, functions, querySelector/addEventListener calls, key handlers, requestAnimationFrame game loop, projectiles, collision, score, and `window.gameState = gameState`. Do not place `const`, `let`, `var`, `function`, `querySelector`, `addEventListener`, or `requestAnimationFrame` after `</script>`, after `</body>`, or after `</html>`. If `write_file` is rejected for JavaScript outside a script tag, do not keep patching fragments; immediately re-emit the entire corrected HTML file from `<!doctype html>` through `</html>` with all JS inside the script block.

Use this for a financial model, budget calculator, ROI/forecast spreadsheet, unit-economics model, or any input-driven calculator.

A gallery craftbook generated from an archetype spec. It runs
`phase → (per-phase gate) → … → evaluate → (loop) → finish`. Each build
phase that produces a checkable artifact is followed by a **runtime
gate-checkpoint** — the runtime verifies the artifact and routes with no
model turn, looping back to redo the phase on a miss. The final `evaluate`
step holds a static deliverable gate plus a reviewer QA pass. What it adds
over the generic `build-loop`: a specialist role per phase, a
domain-correct ordering, and a concrete per-phase quality bar.

2. Build the model (developer) — implement the model with live formulas and labeled cells → gated on `index.html` (html-page)

owning phase to fix named gaps.

# Final paired analysis of the condensed run

The user curtailed the 516-trial plan after results existed. We close out 73 records, using 72 eligible matched trials (18 pairs per model, 16 distinct scenarios, one repetition). The one identity-flagged PowerPoint row stays excluded and unpaired. This is an exploratory chronological subset, not completion of the preregistered design.

Difference = MLX minus llama.cpp; user-selected equivalence margin ±5 percentage points.

| Model | MLX passes | llama.cpp passes | Difference pp | Conservative 95% interval pp | Scenario-cluster 95% interval pp | McNemar nominal / Holm | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma 4 12B Q4 | 16/18 | 18/18 | -11.11 | [-38.09, 20.66] | [-26.32, 0.00] | 0.50 / 1.00 | Inconclusive |
| Qwen 3.8 27B Q4 | 16/18 | 18/18 | -11.11 | [-38.09, 20.66] | [-26.32, 0.00] | 0.50 / 1.00 | Inconclusive |

Each model has 16 both-pass pairs, no both-fail pairs, no MLX-only passes and two llama.cpp-only passes. Neither interval lies inside ±5 pp. Non-significance does not establish equivalence, and the wide interval does not establish a true gap exceeding the margin.

## Assumptions and limits

- Outcome-visible chronological prefix; no random scenario sampling and no completed preregistered design.
- Difference is MLX minus llama.cpp; original user-selected margin remains +/-0.05.
- Conservative paired interval uses Bonferroni-combined 97.5% Clopper-Pearson intervals for each discordance direction. Its nominal coverage assumes independent paired observations; suite overlap violates strict independence.
- 50,000-replicate percentile bootstrap resamples distinct scenario IDs, retaining suite overlap; seed 20261103. Only 16 observed scenario clusters per model, so uncertainty about unseen tasks remains substantial.
- Exact nominal McNemar assumes exchangeable discordance directions under the null and independent discordant pairs. Holm corrects the two model p-values; neither p-value establishes equivalence.
- Both intervals would have to lie strictly within +/-5 pp; neither does. No claim that engines are equivalent or that the true gap exceeds 5 pp.
- Worst-case sensitivity assigns every unavailable original pair a difference of either -1 or +1. It is not a confidence interval.

## Missing evidence and sensitivity

Each original model plan contained 129 pairs. Only 18 are evaluable; 111 are unavailable. No missing outcome is counted as a model failure. Gemma’s PowerPoint pair contains one excluded identity-flagged pass and one unrun counterpart; all other unavailable cells were not run. Full reasons and pair identities are in [the JSON analysis](condensed-paired-analysis.json).

Assigning every unavailable original pair its most unfavorable or favorable possible engine difference gives [−87.60, +84.50] pp for both models. These bounds show how little this prefix can establish about the original full benchmark; they are not confidence intervals.

Within the 72-trial matched subset there are no exclusions. The Qwen productivity conflict-synthesis false-positive is retained as a failure, with its diagnosis in the final scorecard. No scores were changed and no additional trials were selected to obtain a favorable result.

[Final scorecard](final-scorecard.md) · [Scope amendment](scope-amendment.md) · [Original analysis plan](analysis-plan.md) · [Judgments](judging.md)

reports.mlx-prefill-recovery.md:
# MLX prefill recovery and telemetry repair

Recovered 126 observed prefill rates from all 37 recorded MLX trials without running inference. Of those, 121 observations belong to the 36 matched, included MLX trials. The remaining five belong to the identity-flagged, unpaired PowerPoint trial and do not enter comparison aggregates.

| Model | Included MLX trials | Observations | Median of per-trial median prefill rates, tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.8 27B Q4 | 18 | 55 | 604.75 |
| Gemma4 12B Q4 | 18 | 66 | 1332.25 |

These are rounded first-token diagnostic rates, not exact prefill durations or a duration-weighted aggregate of every request. Internal tool-loop requests and cancelled turns may be absent. Time to first token includes work beyond prompt processing, so it cannot safely substitute for pure prefill time. No duration was invented. The scorecard keeps recovered MLX observations in a separate column from llama.cpp's aggregate request timings; these figures alone do not establish that either engine prefills faster.

## Evidence and method

The immutable trial recordings contain `engine_phase` events such as `First token in 19.5s · prefill 819 tok/s`. Only MLX generating-phase diagnostics with this exact provider format were read; generated model text was never interpreted as telemetry. Every retained observation includes its recording line, receive time, session ID and rate in [mlx-prefill-recovery.json](mlx-prefill-recovery.json). Recording and original metrics SHA-256 hashes are included per trial. There were no malformed lines or exact duplicate observations in this recovery.

Within each trial the estimate is the median of observed rates, and the comparison table takes the median across included trial estimates. No trial receives extra aggregate weight because it ran more turns. The parser removes only exact duplicate recorded events. Reconnect replay without stable event IDs cannot be distinguished from a new event, and full request coverage is not asserted.

The [recovery script](recover-mlx-prefill.ts) uses the same [parser as future eval collection](../../src/mlx-prefill-telemetry.ts). The [report generator](finalize-condensed.py) verifies source hashes and reads the separate recovery file. Original `campaign.json`, per-trial `metrics.json`, event recordings, gates, scores, judgments and exclusions remain unchanged. The October 27 campaign was not modified. Earlier derived reports are retained in [report-revisions/pre-mlx-prefill](report-revisions/pre-mlx-prefill/).

## Why ordinary collection lost the data

1. The MLX provider already populated internal `TurnStatsEvent.promptTokensPerSec`, `cachedPromptTokens` and `ttftMs`.
2. Normal chat and one-shot forwarding selected a smaller field set, dropping all three. The public chat schema also omitted them.
3. The remote inference sender, wire schema and receiving session omitted the same fields.
4. The eval collector only parsed daemon logs. MLX's legacy log parser has prompt counts but no prefill duration, so it correctly could not produce an aggregate prefill rate. It never consulted the available event recording.

The source fix forwards all three optional fields through chat and remote inference. The runner now flushes its recorder before collecting metrics, and the collector reads structured `turn_stats` rates into `metrics.mlxPrefill`. It retains source, sample counts and observations, prefers structured terminal samples over historical rounded descriptions, and never mixes the two request boundaries. The existing aggregate `derived.promptTokensPerSec` remains unknown when total timing is unavailable. Normal scorecard reports, CSV exports and per-trial postmortems expose the observed MLX measurements separately.

This repairs telemetry transport and reporting. It does not change model permissions, inference behavior, token accounting, pass/fail classifications or judgments. It applies to subsequent runs using the rebuilt source; it was not retroactively installed into the frozen completed evaluation.

## Updated outputs

- [Final scorecard](final-scorecard.md) and [JSON](final-scorecard.json)
- [Performance CSV](performance.csv) and [audit JSON](performance-audit.json)
- [Recovery observations and provenance](mlx-prefill-recovery.json)
- [Paired conclusions](condensed-paired-analysis.md) and [judgments](judging.md), unchanged in substance

The condensed comparison remains inconclusive for the user-selected ±5 percentage point equivalence margin. Recovering throughput does not alter the 16/18 versus 18/18 pass counts for either model.

reports.analysis-plan.md:
# Predeclared paired MLX / llama.cpp analysis

User selected an equivalence margin of ±5 percentage points on 2026-11-02 (America/Los_Angeles), before any new trial results. MLX minus llama.cpp is the signed difference. This campaign evaluates the integrated engines with their catalog quantizations; it cannot isolate engine code from quantization or speculation.

## Frozen design

Qwen3.8 27B Q4 and Gemma4 12B Q4, both engines, core/productivity/developer/complex-work, three repetitions per suite/scenario/target: expected 516 trials, 129 matched pairs per model. Rotate engine/model order using the existing campaign runner. Pair on model, suite, scenario and repetition. Keep generalist=auto, count-strict, required browser assertions, standard gates, authored timeouts and performance collection. No tuning during the campaign and no rerunning until a favorable p-value appears. Analysis code and scope are recorded before inference.

Use the current clean Gezel revision and rebuilt runtime. Installed Gilde 0.3.5 is unchanged. The campaign source overlay supplies each MLX target its own drafter: Qwen's installed drafter and the previously verified Gemma assistant candidate. Gemma's drafter is not yet part of the installed catalog; this is explicitly a validation of the fixed configuration. llama.cpp keeps its catalog MTP settings. Retain quantization and speculation differences in all reports.

## Primary pass-rate comparison

For each model, report paired sample size, both-pass/both-fail/MLX-only-pass/llama-only-pass counts, pass rates and their signed difference. Produce an exact conditional two-sided McNemar p-value from discordant pairs. Apply Holm correction across the two models. Treat this p-value as a nominal matched-trial analysis: repeated scenarios are not independent evidence about new tasks. A p-value above 0.05 does not prove equivalence.

Report a conservative 95% interval for the pass-rate difference: exact Clopper–Pearson 97.5% two-sided bounds for each directional discordant probability, then [lower(MLX-only)−upper(llama-only), upper(MLX-only)−lower(llama-only)]. Bonferroni coverage is conservative under the independent matched-trial model and gives nonzero uncertainty even with no discordances. Also report a 95% percentile cluster-bootstrap interval (50,000 replicates, seed 20261103), resampling distinct scenario IDs with all their suite appearances and repetitions intact, and computing the pair-weighted difference in each replicate. This cluster interval is approximate and examines sensitivity to task composition. A constant set of cluster differences does not establish zero uncertainty about unseen tasks; flag it explicitly.

Call the fixed-benchmark evidence compatible with practical equivalence only after all planned trials are resolved, the conservative paired interval lies strictly inside [−0.05,+0.05], and the cluster sensitivity interval does too. If cluster resampling is degenerate, limit any equivalence statement to the fixed benchmark and explicitly say generalization remains unestablished. Otherwise report a detected difference or inconclusive evidence; never replace those with “same performance.” This fixed sample can be too small to establish ±5 pp despite a small observed gap. The campaign has no adaptive expansion or early success stopping.

## Missing and excluded trials

Preserve every model failure in the denominator. Exclude only the runner's existing infrastructure/operator/grader ineligibility or comparison issue, with exact evidence and reasons. The primary paired analysis requires both eligible outcomes. List incomplete and excluded pairs separately. Do not infer failure from a missing result. Report worst-case bounds assigning unresolved/excluded pair outcomes both ways; any exclusion makes the headline conditional on evaluable pairs, with no unconditional equivalence claim. No silent retries, changed gates, failure reclassification or mixing older builds.

## Secondary results and quality

Suite comparisons are descriptive. Report fixed scores separately from blinded inline advisory quality, with exact scenario axes and 20 KiB artifact caps. Grade declared artifacts even on failed gates; missing outputs have no invented score. Require full judging reconciliation before final publication/reporting.

For each model/engine/suite report duration, first-token/tool/artifact latencies, actual in-trial decode/prefill rates, token usage, peak process RSS and system memory, including coverage and successful-only sensitivity. Missing telemetry is unknown; macOS GPU utilization is unavailable. Low-token admission probes are not performance estimates. Read logs for discordant outcomes and distinguish model errors from gate/harness/integration failures. Compare prior evidence only in labeled historical sections.

References: [Clopper–Pearson exact intervals](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats._result_classes.BinomTestResult.proportion_ci.html), [NIST McNemar test](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman1/auxillar/mcnemar.htm), [SciPy bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html). Final conclusions are specific to this fixed task distribution and these model builds.
